names.method: I brainstormed about 25 names and shortlisted 12 strong ones from the brainstorm, then checked those plus the 5 earlier candidates, 17 in all, on 2026-10-27. The brainstorm included Teaserwall, Teaserfolio, FigureOne, Figfolio, Paperplate, Labfolio, Specimina, Frontis, Paperbarium, Camready, Arxivogue, Colophon, Vitrine, Folio, Plates, Kata, Abstracta, Splashpage, Preprint Atlas, Exhibit A, Monogram, Paperhaus, Scholarstyle, Labsheen and Colophony. GitHub account existence came from curl https://github.com/<name> (a 200 means a user or org exists, a 404 means none). Repo search used the authenticated gh api search/repositories?q=<name>+in:name. The first pass through the unauthenticated API returned nothing usable because it hit the rate limit. Domains were checked over RDAP. rdap.org rate-limited bulk queries with 429s, so I queried the registries directly: Verisign for .com, Identity Digital for .io, PIR for .org, Google Registry for .dev and .app, and rdap.org with 3 s spacing for .site. The direct CentralNic .site endpoint returned 403. google.io and google.dev both returned 200 as a sanity check. A 200 means registered and a 404 means likely unregistered. I did not check registrar availability or price. The web conflict searches were one or two standard WebSearch queries per name, so obscure conflicts may be missed. The trademark risk ratings are my own judgement; I searched no trademark registry such as USPTO or WIPO.

candidates.name: Teaserbook
candidates.meaning: Earlier candidate: a book of teaser figures/videos from project pages.
candidates.github: github.com/teaserbook returns 404 (no user/org). Repo name search: 0 results.
candidates.web_conflicts: No product found under the exact name. Results were only generic book-teaser content (Teaser Tuesday, book trailers).

candidates.name: ScholarPages
candidates.meaning: Earlier candidate: pages of scholars / academic pages.
candidates.github: github.com/scholarpages returns 404. Repo search: 1 result, Mubuky/ScholarPages (2 stars).
candidates.web_conflicts: No well-known product with this exact name, but the space is crowded with similar names: Scholarly Astro academic theme, OpenScholar, ScholarWorks profiles, academicwebpages.com, plus Google Scholar and Semantic Scholar nearby. The name is generic and easy to confuse.

candidates.name: Project Page Atlas
candidates.meaning: Earlier candidate: an atlas of paper project pages.
candidates.web_conflicts: No exact match. Unrelated 'Project ATLAS' (NCDOT GIS), a Crunchbase 'Project Atlas' and Dragon1 'Atlas Pages' exist. The name is long and descriptive rather than brandable.

candidates.name: Acadero
candidates.meaning: Earlier candidate: coined from academia + Refero.
candidates.github: github.com/acadero returns 200 (a user or org already holds the handle; contents not inspected). Repo search: 0.
candidates.web_conflicts: No product found. The web shows only Spanish near-words (acabadero, asadero, acero). It closely echoes Refero, which the brief says to avoid.

candidates.name: Sitecite
candidates.github: github.com/sitecite returns 200 (account exists). Repo search: 8 results, e.g. RedUhl/SiteCite (2 stars).
candidates.web_conflicts: An existing 'sitecite' Firefox add-on with its own website (quote-and-link tool, self-hostable). WebCite (retired web archiving) is confusable. The name suggests citation tooling, not a design gallery.

candidates.name: Teaserwall
candidates.meaning: A wall of teaser figures and videos, the 'Figure 1' culture of ML project pages.
candidates.web_conflicts: 'Teaserwall' is the name of a content module in the destination.one TYPO3 tourism CMS. No product in design, academic or AI tooling.

candidates.name: Teaserfolio
candidates.meaning: Teaser + portfolio: a portfolio of project-page teasers.
candidates.web_conflicts: No web results for the exact term.

candidates.name: Paperbarium
candidates.meaning: Paper + herbarium: a catalogued specimen collection of paper pages.
candidates.web_conflicts: No exact match. Results were only herbarium-themed decorative paper and baryta (barium) photo paper. It is somewhat hard to parse on first hearing.

candidates.name: FigureOne
candidates.meaning: 'Figure 1', the teaser figure that opens every ML paper and project page.
candidates.github: github.com/figureone returns 200 (account exists). Repo search: 18 results, including airladon/FigureOne (62 stars, a JS library for interactive figures and slides) and deanslee/FigureOneLab (277 stars).
candidates.web_conflicts: Figure 1 (Toronto medical-image community app), Figure 01 humanoid robot from Figure AI, and the FigureOne interactive-figure JS library. These are crowded and confusable in tech and AI.

candidates.name: Figfolio
candidates.meaning: Fig. + portfolio: a folio of figures and pages.
candidates.github: github.com/figfolio returns 404. Repo search: 3 small repos (TylerHarn/FigFolio, siddharth-sundarraman/figfolio, FuJacob/figfolio, all 0 stars).
candidates.web_conflicts: No product found. 'Fig' strongly evokes Figma (.fig files) in the design space, which may confuse readers.

candidates.name: Paperplate
candidates.meaning: Paper + plate (as in a botanical or illustrative plate in a catalogue, or a template boilerplate).
candidates.github: github.com/paperplate returns 200 (account exists). Repo search: 28 results, all tiny (brecert/paperplate, jrmullaney/paperplate, etc.).
candidates.web_conflicts: Pepperplate (recipe app) is confusable, and there is a Labo Paper Plate kids' app. 'Paper plate' as a common household noun is generic and reads as disposable tableware.

candidates.name: Labfolio
candidates.meaning: Lab + portfolio: a lab notebook or portfolio of lab pages.
candidates.github: github.com/labfolio returns 200 (account exists). Repo search: 12 small repos (MakimaBaddie/labfolio, DevYonghunT/Labfolio, hrydaygupta/LabFolio, all 0 stars).
candidates.web_conflicts: Very close to Labfolder (Berlin electronic lab notebook company, Labforward GmbH, widely used in academia, e.g. licensed by the Max Planck Society). It is confusable in academic tooling.

candidates.name: Specimina
candidates.meaning: Latin plural of specimen: type specimens and catalogued samples of page styles.
candidates.github: github.com/specimina returns 404. Repo search: 5 small repos (joesyverson/specimina, EnderKill98/EnderSpecimina 4 stars, an OCR scan repo).
candidates.web_conflicts: No product with the exact name. Specimen Studio (Mannheim design studio on Webflow/Dribbble) and Specim (Finnish hyperspectral imaging) are near-names. The pronunciation is not obvious to everyone.

candidates.name: Frontis
candidates.meaning: Short for frontispiece, the illustrated page facing a book's title page, here the 'front page' of a paper.
candidates.github: github.com/frontis returns 200 (account exists). Repo search: 140 results, dominated by FrontISTR (FEM solver, 119 stars).
candidates.web_conflicts: No direct design or academic product found, but Front (Stockholm design studio), Frontify (brand-guidelines and design-system platform) and Front (customer inbox app) are close. Every major TLD except .site is taken.

candidates.name: Camready
candidates.meaning: Camera-ready: the final accepted version of a paper.
candidates.github: github.com/camready returns 404. Repo search: 4 small repos (vgtomahawk/Charmanteau-CamReady 10 stars, etc.).
candidates.web_conflicts: No product found. Searches return conference camera-ready instructions and MCP-market 'camera-ready prep' skills, so the term may read as a LaTeX or submission tool rather than a web-page gallery. 'Cam' also suggests webcams.

candidates.name: Arxivogue
candidates.meaning: arXiv + vogue: the fashion magazine of preprint web pages.
candidates.web_conflicts: No web results for the exact term. arXiv's brand guidelines say the arXiv name is a registered trademark of arXiv and Cornell University, and they bar using 'arXiv' in non-arXiv project names that imply an official connection.

candidates.name: Colophon
candidates.meaning: The note at the end of a publication describing its typography and production, an exact metaphor for a DESIGN.md.
candidates.github: github.com/colophon returns 200 (account exists). Repo search: 179 results, including colophon-group/jobseek (217 stars) and alphagov/colophon.
candidates.web_conflicts: Colophon Foundry (prominent London type foundry, clients include Instagram and Google), Colophon typeface family by Roy Cole, and countless personal-site '/colophon' pages. This is a strong existing association in typography and design.
